verdict.rationale: Turso's own docs say PITR can restore a database to a specific point in time to recover from user errors such as dropping a table, which covers the core recovery need. Branching from an existing database is also documented. However, the evidence never shows branching at a chosen timestamp or the length of the retention window, so the 'any point within the retention window' part is unproven. Missing for 10: documented retention-window duration/limits, explicit branch-from-timestamp capability, restore workflow details (CLI/API), and independent or hands-on corroboration of PITR.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can restore or branch the database to any point in time within the retention window to recover from bad writes

citations.quote: PITR allows you to restore a database to a specific point in time. This is useful for recovering from user errors, such as dropping a table by mistake.
Turso supports point-in-time recovery (PITR) for databases.
A branch is a separate database instance that is created from an existing database.
